Q16999238.label: Nevis independence referendum
Q16999238.summary: An independence referendum was held in Nevis on 10 August 1998. Although it was approved by 62% of voters, a two-thirds majority was necessary for the referendum to succeed. If it had passed, Nevis would have seceded from the Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis.

Q30632774.label: 2020 Polish presidential election
Q30632774.summary: Presidential elections were held in Poland on 28 June 2020. Q11931462.label: 1954 Czechoslovak parliamentary election
Q11931462.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Czechoslovakia on 28 November 1954. Voters were presented with a single list from the National Front, dominated by the Communist Party of Czechoslovakia (KSČ).

Q290118.label: Party for Bosnia and Herzegovina
Q290118.summary: The Party for Bosnia and Herzegovina is a centre to centre-right political party in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The party is one the most prominent unitarianist parties in the country as it staunchly opposes federalism and devolution of political power along ethnic lines by the means of entities – i.e. Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska.

Q1471814.label: Res Publica Party
Q1471814.summary: Res Publica Party was a political party in Estonia that self-identified as conservative. Established as a party on 8 December 2001, the political organisation Res Publica was founded already as early as 1989 and existed as a community of young conservatives, mostly associated with the Pro Patria Union party during the 1990s. Res Publica was a member of the EPP on the European level. It merged with Pro Patria Union in 2006 to form the Pro Patria and Res Publica Union.

Q181574.label: North American Free Trade Agreement
Q181574.summary: The North American Free Trade Agreement, referred to colloquially in the Anglosphere as NAFTA, was an agreement signed by Canada, Mexico, and the United States that created a trilateral trade bloc in North America.

Q381766.label: 2010 Yushu earthquake
Q381766.summary: The 2010 Yushu earthquake struck on April 14 and registered a magnitude of 6.9 Mw or 7.1 Ms. It originated in Yushu, Qinghai, China, at 7:49 am local time. According to the Xinhua News Agency, 2,698 people were confirmed dead, 270 missing and 12,135 injured, 1,434 of them severely.

Q2069830.label: Operation Seydlitz
Q2069830.desc: German offensive and opposing Soviet defensive operation on the Eastern Front, July 1942
Q2069830.summary: Operation Seydlitz was of an auxiliary nature and was aimed at liberating the zone of the German 9th Army from the penetration of the Soviet 39th Army of Lieutenant General Ivan Maslennikov and the 11th Cavalry Corps of Colonel S. Sokolov.

Q3077958.label: Šiauliai Offensive
Q3077958.desc: summer 1944 battle on Eastern Front of WW2
Q3077958.summary: The Šiauliai offensive was an operation of the Soviet forces of the 1st Baltic Front, commanded by General Hovhannes Bagramyan, conducted from 5 July to 29 August 1944, during the Second World War. It was part of the third phase of the Belorussian strategic offensive operation, and drove German troops from much of Lithuania, with the main tactical objective of the city of Šiauliai.

Q4873030.label: Battle of the Transdanubian Hills
Q4873030.desc: 1945 battle of WWII between Bulgaria and Nazi Germany
Q4873030.summary: The Battle of the Transdanubian Hills was a defensive operation of the Bulgarian First Army during Bulgaria's participation in World War II against German Wehrmacht forces, who were trying to capture the north bank of the Drava river as part of Operation Spring Awakening.

Q282438.label: Battle of Halbe
Q282438.summary: The Battle of Halbe was a battle lasting from April 24 to May 1, 1945, in which the German Ninth Army under the command of General Theodor Busse was destroyed as a fighting force by the advancing Red Army during the Battle of Berlin.

Q592710.label: Revisionist Zionism
Q592710.desc: right-leaning faction of the Zionist movement
Q592710.summary: Revisionist Zionism is a form of Zionism characterized by territorial maximalism. Revisionist Zionism promoted expansionism and the establishment of a Jewish majority on both sides of the Jordan River. Developed by Ze'ev Jabotinsky in the 1920s, Revisionism advocated a "revision" of the "practical Zionism" of David Ben-Gurion and Chaim Weizmann, which was focused on the settling of Eretz Yisrael by independent Jewish individuals.
